haiku-low.q1: They see the generic message "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is written and no mail is sent.
haiku-low.q2: The request is rolled back: nothing is written or sent, and the user gets the same generic "If an account exists" response.
haiku-low.q3: A link lives 30 minutes from creation. It ends sooner when used to reset the password, or when a newer link is issued for the account.
haiku-low.q4: The link stays live: nothing is written when the password fails policy, so it keeps working until expires_at, and the form shows the error.
haiku-low.q5: None. Every session row for that user is deleted, including the resetting device. The user is redirected to /login and signs in with the new password.
haiku-low.q6: The sender retries with backoff up to 3 more times, then logs and drops the job. The user is not notified and can simply request again.
haiku-low.q7: The raw token is generated in API memory and placed in the queued job and the email link (https://app/reset?token=<raw>). Only its SHA-256 hash is stored.
haiku-low.q8: The API SHA-256 hashes the token and selects the pw_reset row with matching token_hash. It must exist, have used_at null, and expires_at in the future. Nothing is written.
haiku-low.q9: In the pw_reset table. The forgot endpoint counts that user's rows with created_at in the last 60 minutes, so older rows fall out of the window as time passes.
haiku-low.q10: Inside the same transaction, after the account lock and rate-limit check, all of the user's still-live tokens get used_at set to now(). They are stamped, not deleted, before the new row is inserted.
haiku-low.q11: In one transaction: the reset row's used_at is stamped, users.password_hash is updated, and that user's sessions rows are deleted, then COMMIT. The confirmation email is queued only after COMMIT.
haiku-low.q12: Only one succeeds because the update is conditional: WHERE id AND used_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now(). If it touches 0 rows, the transaction rolls back and the expired page is shown.

sonnet.q1: They see the same 200 message: "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is written and no mail is sent.
sonnet.q2: Within the transaction, after locking the user's row, the count of pw_reset rows created in the last 60 min (dead ones included) is 3 or more, so it ROLLBACKs. The user gets the same (*1) 200 message, nothing written, nothing sent.
sonnet.q3: 30 minutes (expires_at = created_at + 30 min). It ends sooner if it is used (used_at stamped by a successful reset), or if a newer reset request stamps all the user's live tokens with used_at.
sonnet.q4: Unchanged and still live. Nothing is written, the form returns with the error, and the key keeps working until expires_at.
sonnet.q5: None. All the user's session rows are deleted, including the device they reset from. They are redirected to /login and sign in with the new password; no session is created for them.
sonnet.q6: The sender retries with backoff up to 3 more times, then logs and drops the job. Nobody is notified; the person can just ask again.
sonnet.q7: The raw 32-byte code is generated in API memory, put in the queued job with the link https://app/reset?token=<raw>, and sent by the sender in the email. The job is queued after the (*7) transaction commits and before the 200 response.
sonnet.q8: The API takes ?token=<raw>, hashes it with SHA-256 and selects the reset record whose token_hash matches. The record must exist, have used_at null and an expires_at in the future. Otherwise the user sees the expired page. Nothing is written.
sonnet.q9: In the pw_reset table itself; there is no other rate-limit state. The count covers rows with created_at in the last 60 min, dead ones included. Old requests drop out by aging past 60 minutes, because rows are stamped used and not deleted.
sonnet.q10: In the same transaction as the new request, under the users-row lock, all the user's still-live tokens get used_at = now(). This happens before the new row is inserted, and they are stamped, not deleted.
sonnet.q11: In one transaction: the reset record's used_at is stamped, users.password_hash is updated, and all of that user's sessions rows are deleted. The password-changed email is enqueued only after that COMMIT.
sonnet.q12: The UPDATE on the reset record has WHERE id = row AND used_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now(). Whichever submit gets there first stamps it. The other touches 0 rows, ROLLBACKs and gets the expired page.
